## Generation scripts, in run order

1. `build_master.py` — builds and verifies `human_validation_757_master.csv` from the frozen splits.
2. `build_blinded_sheets.py` — builds the three blinded CSVs (seeds above) from the master.
3. `build_interfaces.py` — builds the three standalone HTML interfaces by embedding each blinded CSV's own review order as JSON.

Not yet run (by design — require real annotation data first): `compute_agreement.py`, `build_adjudication_sheet.py`.

## Blinding confirmation

Checked programmatically in `build_blinded_sheets.py` (asserted, not just visually inspected): each of the three blinded CSVs' columns are exactly `review_id, language, text, sentiment_label, confidence, mixed_sentiment_flag, notes` — the set `{rating, original_label, label_source, source_group_id, word_count}` was checked and confirmed **absent** from every blinded sheet. The same data is what was embedded into each HTML interface (`build_interfaces.py` reads directly from the blinded CSVs, not from the master), so the interfaces inherit the same guarantee — no rating, original label, model prediction, or model confidence is present anywhere in the annotator-facing files or the interfaces' embedded JSON.

Each of the three `*_blinded.csv` files was also confirmed, at generation time, to have **zero non-blank values** across `sentiment_label`, `confidence`, `mixed_sentiment_flag`, and `notes` — nothing was pre-filled.

## What remains to be confirmed once annotation begins

- That each annotator's browser-local progress persistence behaves as designed (localStorage keyed by `sentiment_annotation_<annotator_id>_v1` — distinct keys per annotator prevent any cross-contamination even if, as can happen under the `file://` protocol in some browsers, multiple local HTML files share a single storage origin).
- That the exported CSV from each interface preserves `review_id` exactly and can be merged back to the master purely by that key, independent of each annotator's distinct display order — this is enforced by `build_interfaces.py`'s export logic, which always writes rows in a fixed canonical (alphabetically sorted by `review_id`) order regardless of the order reviews were shown in, but has not yet been exercised against a real completed round.
